title: Pixel build
suits: games, creator tools, dev tools with a playful streak, kids and education, indie apps: anything that wants to feel handmade, fun and a bit nostalgic

params.--field: the sky gradient; it is dithered into bands and the pixel ranges are built from its stops
params.--brand: the blocks of the mark (with light and dark bevel tints)
params.--brand-2: the critter, and the blocks of the mark's last stroke when it is a small accent
params.__MARK__: stroke paths in a 24 x 24 box, rasterised to a 12 x 12 block grid; an empty mark falls back to a block tile with the first letter
params.__WORD__: set in a hand-drawn bitmap face that shrinks to fit

details: the whole reveal runs on a 15 fps sprite clock, so motion steps like a real 8-bit game
blocks drop row by row from the bottom of the mark up, like a stacking game
each block lands with a two-frame squash
the bottom row kicks up pixel dust
the wordmark fizzles in pixel by pixel in a hand-drawn bitmap face, not a font
the word's drop shadow arrives one frame late
a tiny critter fizzles in on the last letter, hops across the word and lands on the mark's last block
the block squashes under the critter's weight
the critter blinks once it has settled
the sky is dithered into bands, with pixel ranges on the horizon built from the field's own stops
a dark sky gets pixel stars, a lit one three flat pixel clouds
the mark is rasterised at load, so any line mark becomes chunky pixel art with close strokes kept apart
a small last stroke (a dot, a slash) is picked out in the accent colour
